name: Binance
verdict: OAuth is only for close ecosystem partners after contacting Binance's business team, likely taking months. Without it, each user creates their own API key (ideally read-only, no withdrawals) and pastes it in, workable the same day.
needGuide: Yes — decide whether a partnership is realistic; otherwise use user-supplied API keys.

auth.detail: Everyday access is user-created API keys (requests signed with HMAC, RSA or Ed25519; Ed25519 preferred), with no OAuth. Binance Login (OAuth 2.0) exists: authorize at accounts.binance.com/en/oauth/authorize, token at POST accounts.binance.com/oauth/token, authorization code flow for web apps and PKCE (S256) for native apps, refresh_token grant supported; example scopes user:openId, create:apikey, read. The docs say it is 'exclusively offered to close ecosystem partners'. Binance's own MCP server uses OAuth client IDs for named AI clients, with user-chosen scopes and no withdrawal scope.

effort.timeToFirstTest: 1–2 hours with an API key against the Spot Testnet; OAuth: unknown
effort.timeToProduction: unknown (partner negotiation; likely months for OAuth) | same day via user-supplied API keys

approval.gate: OAuth: contact Binance's business team and be accepted as a close ecosystem partner; no self-serve public listing was found. Without it, each user creates their own API key and pastes it into your app. Binance Connect 2.0 and Binance Pay technical-service-provider authorization also appear in the docs index and look partner-oriented (unread).

scopes.why: Per-key permission toggles (read, trading, withdrawals); the OAuth scope list wasn't available.
scopes.summary: API keys: permission toggles per key (reading, spot/margin trading, withdrawals and others), so request read-only. OAuth: scopes passed comma-separated (user:openId, create:apikey, read); the full scope list page was empty when fetched.

cost: API keys free; partner terms unknown
prerequisites: Account and owner: A company-owned Binance entity (business) account is needed to create an OAuth app in the Developer Center; business verification is likely required. Someone with authority for a partnership conversation.

Where you register: Binance Developer Center → sign in with a Binance entity account → create an OAuth application (client ID and secret), but only after contacting the Binance business team. API-key path: user's Binance account → API Management (likely).
Cost: API keys free; partner terms unknown

registerAt.path: Binance Developer Center → sign in with a Binance entity account → create an OAuth application (client ID and secret), but only after contacting the Binance business team. API-key path: user's Binance account → API Management (likely).

steps.do: Decide the path: user-supplied API keys now, Binance Login OAuth only if a partnership is realistic
Build the key-entry screen telling users to create a read-only API key with no withdrawals and IP restriction
Store keys encrypted; validate with a signed read call; use Ed25519 and percent-encode the payload before signing
Test against testnet.binance.vision with Testnet keys
If pursuing OAuth: contact the Binance business team, then create the OAuth app in the Developer Center with an entity account
Implement authorization code plus PKCE and refresh handling

roles.team: A company-owned Binance entity (business) account is needed to create an OAuth app in the Developer Center; business verification is likely required. Someone with authority for a partnership conversation.
roles.customer: The Binance user approves the consent screen (OAuth) or creates the API key themselves, ideally read-only with no withdrawal permission and an IP allowlist (likely).

testing: Spot Testnet at testnet.binance.vision and a Demo Mode are documented; both use separate keys.

blockers.problem: Binance Login is restricted to close ecosystem partners
blockers.fix: Fall back to user-supplied API keys.
Percent-encode before signing (effective around 2026-01-15) or requests fail with -1022 INVALID_SIGNATURE.

blockers.problem: Holding user trading keys is a high-risk liability
blockers.fix: Require read-only keys and encrypt at rest.

blockers.problem: Regional Binance entities may have separate docs and keys
blockers.fix: Confirm which one your users are on.

automation.agentCan: Write signing and validation code, the key-entry UI and test calls, and draft the partnership outreach and use-case description.
automation.humanMust: Business account creation and verification, contacting and negotiating with Binance's business team, legal agreements, and each user creating their own API key with 2FA.

uncertain: Partner eligibility criteria and timeline, refresh token lifetime, the full OAuth scope list, Binance Connect 2.0 details (pages would not load), business-verification requirements, regional (Binance.US) differences.
